questions.problem:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $b,$ given by 

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -4 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $2\times 2$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $y$ such that 

$$
{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to $Ax=b.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -4 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=2 \\ -4{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is ${y}_{1}=2$ and ${y}_{2}=6.$ 

Therefore, $y=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 6\end{aligned}].$

questions.problem:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $b,$ given by 

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -4 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $3\times 3$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $y$ such that

$$
{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to $Ax=b.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -4 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2} \\ {y}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -1 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=-2 \\ {y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=-1 \\ -{y}_{1}-4{y}_{2}+{y}_{3}=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the solution to this system using forward substitution, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & =-2, \\ {y}_{2} & =-1-{y}_{1} \\  & =-1-(-2) \\  & =1, \\ {y}_{3} & =-3+4{y}_{2}+{y}_{1} \\  & =-3+4(1)+(-2) \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 
$y=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

questions.problem:
Consider the LU decomposition of the matrix $A$ and the vector $b,$ given by

$$
A={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U},\,b=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 20\end{aligned}].
$$

If $⟨{x}_{1},{x}_{2}⟩$ and $⟨{y}_{1},{y}_{2}⟩$ are the solutions to the systems $Ax=b$ and $Ly=b$ respectively, what is the value of ${x}_{2}\cdot {y}_{2}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the two systems in turn.

- First, we solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=b=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 20\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=6 \\ 4{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=20.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is ${y}_{1}=6$ and ${y}_{2}=-4.$ Therefore, 

$$
y=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -4\end{aligned}].
$$

- Next, we solve $Ux=y.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=y=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -4\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=6 \\ 4{x}_{2}=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is ${x}_{2}=-1$ and ${x}_{1}=\frac{5}{2}.$ Therefore, 

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{2} \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, ${x}_{2}\cdot {y}_{2}=(-1)\cdot (-4)=4.$

[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=b=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=5 \\ -2{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=4.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is ${y}_{1}=5$ and ${y}_{2}=14.$ Therefore, 

$$
y=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 14\end{aligned}].
$$

$$
[\begin{aligned}7 & 3 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=y=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 14\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}7{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=5 \\ -2{x}_{2}=14.\end{aligned}

$$

questions.problem:
Consider the LU decomposition of the matrix $A$ and the vector $b,$ given by

$$
A={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U},\,b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

If $⟨{x}_{1},{x}_{2}⟩$ and $⟨{y}_{1},{y}_{2}⟩$ are the solutions to the systems $Ax=b$ and $Ly=b$ respectively, what is the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {y}_{1}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the two systems in turn.

- First, we solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=-1 \\ -{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=3.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is ${y}_{1}=-1$ and ${y}_{2}=2.$ Therefore, 

$$
y=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

- Next, we solve $Ux=y.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=y=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=-1 \\ {x}_{2}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is ${x}_{2}=2$ and ${x}_{1}=-1.$ Therefore, 

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, ${x}_{1}\cdot {y}_{1}=(-1)\cdot (-1)=1.$
